question.text: A calorimeter of water equivalent <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of water at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><none></none><mo>'</mo><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>'</mo></mmultiscripts></math>' grams of steam at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is mixed in it till the temperature of the mixture is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>31</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><none></none><mo>'</mo><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>'</mo></mmultiscripts></math> is close to (Latent heat of water<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mn>540</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, specific heat of water<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>°</mo></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
